entities.summary: Fàn Zhěn was a Chinese philosopher, politician, and writer who lived during the Classical era of Chinese history. As an atheist of the Southern Qi Dynasty, he is remembered today for his treatise Shén Miè Lùn, which was preserved in the Book of Liang. This work challenged traditional Confucian beliefs and influenced the development of Neo-Confucianism. Fàn Zhěn's ideas also resonated with later thinkers, such as Zhu Xi, who built upon his concepts. Fàn Zhěn's significance lies in his ability to provoke a critical examination of the dominant philosophical framework of his time, leading to a more nuanced understanding of the human condition. His ideas have had a lasting impact on Chinese intellectual history and continue to be studied by scholars today.
